Characteristic-zero Hecke actions include the full rational first-coefficient pairing. R13.4a→R12.3→R12.6→R13.4b is preserved. nodes.title: The normalized lattice Weierstrass model
nodes.statement: For a native PeriodPair L, define W_L with a₁=a₂=a₃=0, a₄=−L.g₂/4 and a₆=−L.g₃/4. Its discriminant is L.g₂³−27L.g₃² and is nonzero. The projective map z↦[℘_L(z):℘′_L(z)/2:1] off the lattice extends across each lattice point by O=[0:1:0] and descends to a pointed biholomorphism C/L.lattice ≅ W_L^an. It intertwines addition with the algebraic group law.
hypotheses: The lattice has rank two over Z and spans C over R. Its orientation is not part of PeriodPair; choose an oriented basis only when normalizing to H.
Projective affine coordinates use the native Weierstrass equation y²=x³−g₂x/4−g₃/4. Totalized native ℘ values at a pole are not projective coordinates.
proofSteps: Use the native differential equation away from the lattice. Laurent expansions ℘=z⁻²+O(z²), ℘′=−2z⁻³+O(z) give the projective extension at O.

Count zeros of the elliptic function ℘−x to obtain a two-sheeted x-map and injectivity once ℘′ is included. Its three nonzero half-periods have distinct x-values; hence the cubic discriminant is nonzero.
Periodicity descends the map; compactness and the local charts show it is a biholomorphism. The explicit ℘ addition formula identifies the group laws.

nodes.title: Pointed elliptic uniformization
nodes.statement: For a smooth projective Weierstrass elliptic curve E/C with identity O, the analytification supplied by the shared carrier is a compact connected one-dimensional complex Lie group. There is a rank-two discrete lattice Λ⊂C and a pointed holomorphic group isomorphism C/Λ→E^an. Conversely every such lattice is realized by the preceding Weierstrass model. Isomorphisms of pointed elliptic curves correspond to nonzero homotheties uΛ=Λ′; general holomorphic group homomorphisms correspond to complex-linear maps z↦uz with uΛ⊂Λ′, including u=0. Algebraic and analytic pointed morphisms agree.
hypotheses: E is smooth, projective, geometrically connected of genus one, with its algebraic group law.
Use the projective points dictionary, not only the affine solution set.
proofSteps: Analytify the smooth projective curve and its group maps. Proper coherent comparison gives H⁰(E^an,O)=C, hence connectedness, and compact-surface cohomology identifies its analytic genus as one; choose the nonzero algebraic invariant differential ω.

Integrate ω around an oriented integral homology basis. The bilinear relation and positivity of iω∧conjugate(ω) make its two periods real-linearly independent. Integration from O defines E^an→C/Λ; it is a local isomorphism since ω never vanishes. Compactness and connectedness make it a covering onto the torus. Its induced homology image is the whole period lattice by definition, hence the covering has degree one. Invariance of ω identifies the group law.

Use the explicit lattice Weierstrass map for the inverse construction. Lift pointed group maps to the universal covers; their additive holomorphic lifts are complex-linear. Proper-source morphism comparison algebraizes maps between the proper algebraic curves.

nodes.title: Projective full level in the Bakker–Tsimerman setting
nodes.statement: For a prime p>3, take strict full p-frames modulo simultaneous multiplication by F_p^×. Their determinant values modulo squares give two geometric components. Each coarse component is the compactification of the effective Γ(p) quotient. The projective-frame stack has generic μ₂ inertia; rigidifying that central μ₂ gives the smooth full-level curve for p>3. Its forgetful quotient by the effective deck group is the (2,3,p) orbifold on the rigidified bare-polygon moduli stack: the quotient map has elliptic branch orders 2 and 3 and boundary order p. On a strict full p-component the effective index is (p³−p)/2, the number of cusps is (p²−1)/2 and the genus is (p+2)(p−3)(p−5)/24. These are applications of MF10A/10B, not new dimension-formula targets.

nodes.title: Torsion congruences and level extension

nodes.title: Fine loci and bad-level inertia
nodes.statement: The compact full-level stack over Z is a fine scheme for N≥2 unless N is a prime power p^s or twice a prime power 2p^s; N=1 is an additional nonfine case. A sufficient fine condition for compact Γ₁(N) over a base is that N have an invertible divisor d≥5 on that base; the open complex fine range N≥4 is not substituted at cusps.
